did_you_know.text: The vision shows Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, while Satan stands at his right hand to accuse him.
The Lord rebukes Satan and protects not only Joshua but also Jerusalem, which is referred to in the verse as “the one who has chosen Jerusalem.”
Joshua is described as “a brand plucked from the fire”—a burning ember or piece of wood rescued from the flames. This image represents deliverance from danger or destruction.
Joshua is dressed in filthy garments, symbolizing his unworthy condition before he is cleansed.

The angel commands that Joshua’s filthy garments be removed and declares, “I have taken away your iniquity.” He then commands that Joshua be dressed in fine garments—that is, clean and ceremonial clothing.
In addition to the new garments, a clean turban is placed on Joshua’s head, and he is redressed in the presence of the angel of the Lord.
Joshua’s position depends on his faithfulness: he must walk in the Lord’s ways, keep his charge, govern the house of the Lord, and guard its courts.
Joshua and his fellow priests are called “men of sign,” and they are presented as a sign of something the Lord is about to bring in the future.
Before Joshua lies a stone with seven eyes, and the Lord says that he will open it and remove the iniquity of that land in a single day.
The vision ends with a picture of peace and security: people will invite one another to sit under their vines and fig trees.
